home.lead: DDNS, STUN NAT traversal, port forwarding, reverse proxy, certificates, WAF, Tailscale and frp, all in a single ~22 MB binary. Runs on home networks, NAS boxes, cloud hosts and servers of every kind.

home.featuresTitle: The everyday network toolbox, managed in one place
home.featuresDesc: Covers the features home networks and server ops rely on most. Every module can be enabled or disabled on its own.

features.title: Dynamic DNS
features.text: 11 providers including Alibaba Cloud, Cloudflare, Tencent Cloud, DNSPod, Huawei Cloud and GoDaddy; detect your IP by URL, network interface or command, IPv4 and IPv6, webhook notifications.

features.title: STUN Traversal
features.text: TCP / UDP hole punching and keep-alive, UPnP / NAT-PMP, built-in forwarding; triggers webhooks and scripts when the public address changes.

features.title: Port Forwarding
features.text: TCP / UDP, IPv4 / IPv6, port ranges, multi-target failover, connection limits and traffic statistics.

features.title: SSL Certificates
features.text: Automatic ACME DNS-01 issuance and renewal with wildcard and EAB support; map certificates to a directory and run a script after changes.

features.title: Web Services
features.text: Per-domain reverse proxy, redirects and static files; HTTPS, WebSocket and PROXY protocol; weighted multi-backend policies, health checks, compression, rate limiting and response caching.

features.title: WAF Firewall
features.text: Built-in Coraza and OWASP CRS v4, rules enabled per file, custom SecLang support, block or detect-only mode.

features.title: Networking & Tunnels
features.text: Supervises Tailscale, frp (frpc / frps) and cloudflared tunnels as managed processes, always using the latest upstream release.

features.title: Docker Management
features.text: Create and edit containers, logs and terminals, Compose, image updates with one-click upgrade (automatic rollback on failure), networks and volumes.

features.title: Web Terminal
features.text: SSH, Telnet and a local shell (disabled by default) with proxy support, persistent sessions, SFTP file management and split panes.

features.title: File Services
features.text: WebDAV and FTP services plus storage management, with local and remote WebDAV mounts and online file management.

features.title: Scheduled Tasks & Wake-on-LAN
features.text: Cron jobs that run commands or HTTP requests and keep run history; Wake-on-LAN magic packet broadcast and online probing.

features.title: Security Hardening
features.text: Two-factor authentication, login rate limiting, secure entrance path, LAN-only access, HTTPS for the admin UI and API tokens.

features.title: Access Control
features.text: Per-site path rules, temporary share links, automatic bans on repeated auth failures, GeoIP country filtering and IP allow/block lists.

features.title: Traffic Stats & Monitoring
features.text: Per-minute access and traffic statistics, exposed as Prometheus metrics for your existing monitoring stack.

features.title: Notification Center
features.text: Webhook, Telegram, Bark, WeCom, DingTalk, Feishu and email; push by severity and event rules, with silencing and de-duplication.

features.title: Configuration Backup
features.text: Encrypted backups (scrypt + AES-GCM), retention policies and scheduled backups to a local directory or a storage mount.

features.title: Network Diagnostics
features.text: Ping, traceroute, port probing, DNS lookup, speed test and LAN scan, all run as background tasks.

features.title: API, CLI & MCP
features.text: Multiple tokens with per-module permissions and auto-generated OpenAPI docs; use gately ctl to drive an instance and gately mcp to connect AI assistants.

home.promisesTitle: Software on your network edge should be easy to see through
home.promisesDesc: It holds your DNS keys and certificate private keys, so every behavior should be open to inspection.

promises.title: Transparent
promises.text: No connections to project servers and no device reporting by default. Every outbound address, such as public IP lookup and STUN servers, is visible, editable and can be turned off.

promises.title: Auditable
promises.text: Configuration is plain JSON with 0600 permissions, ready for git diffs and rollbacks. Sensitive fields are masked in API output.

promises.title: In your control
promises.text: Third-party sign-in uses OAuth apps you register yourself, with no relay in between. There is no built-in self-update; upgrades come from Docker or your package manager.

promises.title: Single-file deployment
promises.text: One static binary with the frontend embedded. Runs under Docker, systemd and OpenWrt, covering NAS, soft routers and cloud hosts.

home.installTitle: Up and running in a minute
home.installDesc: Images are available for amd64, arm64 and arm/v7. After starting, open http://DEVICE_IP:16680 and sign in as admin with the initial password from the logs.
home.installDocker:
docker run -d --name gately --network host \
  -v ./gately-data:/etc/gately \
  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  ghcr.io/wangwanjie/gately:latest
docker logs gately 2>&1 | grep -i "initial password"
home.installBinary:
# Download the archive for your platform from Releases and extract it
./gately -c /etc/gately

# The admin UI listens on :16680 by default
# Username admin; the initial password is printed in the startup log

faqs.q: Can I migrate my existing Lucky configuration directly?
faqs.a: Yes. Under Settings → Backup & Migration, choose a .lkcf file or a whole-site config zip, preview it, then import. Imported rules are disabled by default, so you can run alongside Lucky, switch over module by module and roll back at any time.

faqs.q: Does it need to connect to your servers?
faqs.a: No. Gately does not connect to any project servers by default and reports nothing.

faqs.q: Which devices can it run on?
faqs.a: Home NAS, soft routers, cloud hosts and servers of all kinds. Binaries are provided for Linux (amd64 / arm64 / arm / mips / mipsle / riscv64), macOS, Windows and FreeBSD, plus Docker images for amd64 / arm64 / arm/v7.

faqs.q: Why is host networking recommended for port forwarding and STUN?
faqs.a: These modules listen directly on host ports. If you do not need Docker management, you can drop the docker.sock mount.
